reason: Flaky: page.frames lags the iframe's load event on Chromium and stock WebKit in a loaded run (one hit each)

Asserts frames' names (the `name` attribute, as `frame.name()` reports it, with the tree's nesting). Strider's frame tree has a `name` field, but no backend reports a frame's name, so it is always `None`. The matrix row says `has`, which holds only for the tree, not for names
`frame.page()` returns the page a frame belongs to. Strider's frame locators are entered from a page but carry no reference back to it, so there's no read that returns the page
The original skips Firefox (`it.skip(browserName === 'firefox')`): Firefox words its refusal of a frame that sets `X-Frame-Options` differently, and the test looks for Chromium's and WebKit's text
Unsupported: Strider refuses navigation.sameDocument on stock WebKit: stock WebKit) (stock WebKit's inspector reports no same-document navigation
Subframe navigation requests are missing from the history on WebKit
Firefox: a child frame's URL and navigations reach the model after the iframe's own load event
Browser-generated console messages (a frame refused by X-Frame-Options) are never reported on Chromium, and aren't on WebKit
